newsitem.title: UK: Good demand boosts N.Sea crude, paper firm, quiet.
newsitem.headline: Good demand boosts N.Sea crude, paper firm, quiet.

text.p: North Sea physical crude markets traded firmer led by stronger wet Brent on Monday while paper values looked robust but volume was modest, traders said.
"Margins are getting crushed and the end-users are not happy. But it doesn't seem to be a serious brake on the buying yet," one wet market analyst said.
"It looks tidy on physical. There are not too many (cargoes) around. It favours the sellers," a trader said.

The outright price came off from morning levels, with the front-month August IPE contract trading at $17.75 a barrel at 1800 GMT. This was eight cents firmer than Friday but 20 cents down from midday in sympathy with weaker New York values.
Good demand from a crowd of wet Brent shorts raised the value of a July 5-7 loader to August Brent -19 cents, eight cents above the price paid for the cargo on Friday.
The previous reported Brent trade was a June 26-28 stem moved at August Brent -60 cents early last week.
A Gullfaks C loading July 8-10 moved at around seven cents firmer at Dated Brent +30 cents, while an Ekofisk loading the same dates move at the unchanged value of Dated Brent +20 cents.
One player said he had heard the Ekofisk's real value was Dated +22 but he had no details.

"One might have thought the offshore grades might have come off with freight rates coming down but the buying has held them up," the analyst said. A Forties loading July 9-11 was heard changing hands but th trade was private and confidential.
